proposal.description_long: Robert I. Friedman’s Red Mafiya was published in 2000. Hachette identifies it as a book about Russian criminal networks, and a 2000 New York Review of Books review describes their activity across countries and their presence in Israel. The review cites an FBI report that most members of one Russian criminal organization had Israeli passports and quotes a former State Department official saying the Russian organized-crime figures tracked by the department also carried Israeli passports. The reviewer characterizes the book as an exposé but cautions that it has no notes, making some of Friedman’s dramatic findings difficult to verify, and says some accusations might not stand in a criminal case. The linked New York Times archive is a separate report about money laundering in Israel and the Bank of New York investigation; it does not quote Friedman. The TrumpFile entry itself says the exact quotation was pending and identifies no connection to Donald Trump. This draft summarizes the book’s documented subject and review, while recommending exclusion from a Trump-specific chronology unless a Trump nexus is sourced.
